title: The Eclipse and the Stork
explanation:
# Animal Reactions to a Total Solar Eclipse

When the Moon completely blocks the Sun during a total eclipse, animals are fooled into thinking night has arrived in the middle of the day—causing crickets and frogs to sing their nighttime songs, fireflies to glow, and birds to fall silent as ducks settle onto one leg to sleep. As soon as sunlight returns and totality ends, songbirds burst into their dawn chorus, the nocturnal creatures go quiet, and life snaps back to normal, leaving animals and people briefly bewildered by nature's cosmic sleight of hand.
